title: api: fix remote manifest add --artifact without storage driver set
body:
ManifestModify stores uploaded artifact files under <graphroot>/<driver>-images/<list ID>, but it took the driver name from runtime.StorageConfig().GraphDriverName.  That is the configured driver, which is empty when storage.conf does not set one (e.g. openSUSE Tumbleweed), even though the store auto-selects a driver.  The path became <graphroot>/-images/<list ID>, which does not exist, so "podman-remote manifest add --artifact" failed with HTTP 400.

Add Runtime.GraphDriver(), which returns the driver actually in use, and use it to build the path.

Fixes: https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/30280
